title.narrative: Welang River Basin – Participatory design of river basin interventions

description.narrative: The Welang River Basin Transformation Project was a collaborative initiative between the Governments of Indonesia and the Netherlands that addressed critical water management challenges in the Welang River Basin, East Java. Rapid urbanisation and economic growth had intensified flooding, erosion, sedimentation, and water distribution issues, underscoring the need for an integrated and resilient approach. Financed by the Partners for Water programme, the project applied a multi-stakeholder, co-creation methodology to deliver sustainable, locally driven solutions aligned with Indonesia’s water management framework and suitable for replication.The collaborative initiative started in 2020. In phase I (PVW4A20018), a river basin inventory and baseline assessment was conducted, including a master planning process. Phase II (2023-2024) focused on detailing downstream and midstream interventions through a co-creation and participatory design process.Phase II consisted of three subphases: an inception phase focused on stakeholder engagement, site selection, and basin-level planning; a co-creation and design phase in which solutions were developed and tested through pilot projects; and a final phase that produced a roadmap for long-term implementation and upscaling. Four pilot sites represented the basin’s diverse challenges. Welang Lama and Sidogiri addressed recurrent flooding through a combination of dykes, bypass channels, retention basins, waste management, and early warning systems. Upstream pilots at Wonosari Tea Plantation and Surorowo focused on water retention, soil erosion control, and nature-based solutions that supported sustainable agriculture.A core achievement of the project was its co-creation approach, which actively involved communities, landowners, and government agencies throughout design and implementation. By combining structural and non-structural measures, the initiative strengthened water safety, reduced flood risks, and built local capacity. The project has since been recognised by central government and international financing institutions as a leading example of sustainable, catchment-level water management with strong potential for replication across Java and beyond. In the upstream catchment various small-scale Nature-based Solutions (NbS) were selected and implemented by local communities and private sector. The initiative has been captured in a project video. A miniseries of articles was drafted to highlight different components of the approach taken in Welang. Both are attached in this projects' media library.The overall objective of this project is expressed in five sub objectives:1. Three conceptual designs for multifunction demonstration-sites.2. Improved valuing of the Welang River; increased societal awareness, contributing to behavior change.3. Improved EJP absorbing and executing capacity.4. Improved inter-governmental coordination.5. Improved inter-office coordination.
